title: 两点半前烤蛋糕  (Four Cakes by Half Past Two)

segments.t: Ten seconds later in the warm cafe kitchen, Mei and Peng are calmly shelling almonds when Qing rushes through the swinging door holding up three fingers. Let us listen in first.
车站刚发来紧急消息：老地图师今天下午三点整就到！
下午三点？！志鹏，立刻把两台烤箱拧到烘焙温度！
两个开关都打开了！小美，四个莓果杏仁蛋糕烤好再晾凉最快要多久？
烤四十分钟，晾凉三十分钟，刷暖蜂蜜糖釉十分钟！
这么算正好两点二十五分——还宽裕三十五分钟呢！
我给四个圆烤盘抹黄油，小美你来打鸡蛋！
小晴，把那四碗新鲜夏莓洗干净，再用亚麻布轻轻吸干水分！
洗得又快又轻！幸亏咱们星期天把三种糖釉都试了一遍！
真不敢想今天三点端出第一炉铜器亮光剂或者第二炉屋顶瓦片会怎样！
志鹏，少贫嘴，手快点儿——把磨好的杏仁粉顺滑地拌进去！
等等——听见老陈在大堂喊我名字了吗？房卡钥匙那边出事了！
小晴，快去救前台吧；两点半之前这间厨房归我和志鹏管！
Now let's go through it line by line with the English translation.
车站刚发来紧急消息：老地图师今天下午三点整就到！

'Urgent bulletin straight from the station: our mapmaker arrives at three sharp today!' "Jinji" (urgent) pairs with "xiaoxi" (news) for an emergency bulletin, while "sandian zheng" marks three on the dot.
下午三点？！志鹏，立刻把两台烤箱拧到烘焙温度！
'Three in the afternoon?! Peng, crank both ovens up to baking temperature this second!' Turning a dial uses "ning dao" ("twist up to"), while "hongbei wendu" literally means baking temperature.
两个开关都打开了！小美，四个莓果杏仁蛋糕烤好再晾凉最快要多久？

'Both switches are on! Mei, how fast can four berry almond cakes bake and cool down?' In "kaohao zai liangliang", "liangliang" means to let hot baked goods air-cool, and "zuikuai yao duojiu" asks "what's the fastest it takes?"
烤四十分钟，晾凉三十分钟，刷暖蜂蜜糖釉十分钟！
'Forty minutes to bake, thirty minutes to cool, and ten minutes for warm honey glaze!' Brushing a sweet glaze on top uses "shua" ("brush on"), with "fengmi tangyou" meaning honey sugar glaze.
这么算正好两点二十五分——还宽裕三十五分钟呢！
'That brings us right to two twenty-five—with thirty-five minutes to spare!' "Kuanyu" describes comfortable breathing room in time or money—here meaning plenty of spare minutes left over.
我给四个圆烤盘抹黄油，小美你来打鸡蛋！
'I'll butter all four round cake pans while you whisk the eggs, Mei!' Peng uses "mo" for smearing butter inside a pan, while "jidan" (eggs) pairs with "da" in the kitchen phrase for beating eggs.
小晴，把那四碗新鲜夏莓洗干净，再用亚麻布轻轻吸干水分！

'Qing, rinse those four bowls of fresh summer berries and gently blot them dry with linen!' "Xigan shuifen" combines "xi" ("absorb/blot") + "gan" ("dry") to mean soaking moisture gently off delicate fruit.
洗得又快又轻！幸亏咱们星期天把三种糖釉都试了一遍！

'Washing fast and gentle! Thank goodness we tested all three glazes on Sunday!' "Xingkui" opens with grateful relief ("thank goodness"), while "shi le yi bian" means testing through the whole batch once.
真不敢想今天三点端出第一炉铜器亮光剂或者第二炉屋顶瓦片会怎样！
'Just imagine serving Batch One brass polish or Batch Two roof tiles at three today!' Baking batches take the counter "lu" ("diyi lu", first oven batch), from the character meaning stove or oven.
志鹏，少贫嘴，手快点儿——把磨好的杏仁粉顺滑地拌进去！

'Less wisecracking and faster whisking, Peng—fold the ground almond meal in smoothly!' Teasing word "pinzui" means talking cheeky nonsense or joking around, and "ban jinqu" means to fold gently into batter.
等等——听见老陈在大堂喊我名字了吗？房卡钥匙那边出事了！

'Wait—do you hear Chen shouting my name from the lobby? Something's up with the room keys!' Qing says "han" for shouting someone's name across a room, and "chushi" alerts everyone that trouble popped up.
小晴，快去救前台吧；两点半之前这间厨房归我和志鹏管！
'Go rescue the front desk, Qing; Peng and I have this kitchen covered until two-thirty!' "Gui ... guan" means "under someone's charge"—Mei claims full command of the kitchen until half past two.
Now let's listen to the whole conversation one last time.

Both ovens roar to life in Mei and Peng's capable hands while Qing dashes back to solve a front-desk key mystery. See you next time.
再见！
